title: The Limits of Automatic Evaluation of Creativity in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.23705v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly capable of generating text that challenges human performance in domains requiring creativity, yet evaluating creativity in LLM-generated content remains a significant challenge. Here, we investigate whether current automatic evaluation methods can reliably capture human judgments of creativity. We collect human evaluations of human- and AI-generated short stories from the WritingPrompts dataset across 11 dimensions of creativity, and compare these judgments with automated objective metrics and LLM-as-a-Judge evaluations. Our experiments reveal substantial misalignment between automatic evaluations and human assessments. In particular, LLM-based judges exhibit a systematic preference for AI-generated stories, consistently favoring their stylistic characteristics over the unpredictability and other qualities of human-authored texts. translated_title: 大型语言模型创造力自动评估的局限性
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）在需要创造力的领域中生成文本的能力日益增强，甚至挑战人类表现，但评估LLM生成内容中的创造力仍是一项重大挑战。在此，我们研究当前自动评估方法是否能可靠地捕捉人类对创造力的判断。我们从WritingPrompts数据集中收集了人类对人工和AI生成的短篇小说在11个创造力维度上的评估，并将这些判断与自动化客观指标和LLM作为评判者的评估进行比较。我们的实验揭示了自动评估与人类评估之间的显著不一致。特别是，基于LLM的评判者表现出对AI生成故事的系统性偏好，始终偏爱其风格特征，而非人类作者文本的不可预测性及其他品质。此外，相关性分析显示，广泛使用的自动评估指标与人类判断的关联有限。
tldr: 本研究发现，现有的自动评估方法，尤其是基于LLM的评判者，无法可靠地匹配人类对创造力的判断，并表现出对AI生成文本的系统性偏好。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that current automatic evaluation methods, especially LLM-based judges, fail to reliably align with human creativity judgments and show a systematic preference for AI-generated text.
